scorecard.name: Branding and Survey Check
scorecard.coaching: Agent omitted mandatory closing branding 'thank you for choosing s-net' and customer satisfaction survey request.

scorecard.name: Verified customer
scorecard.coaching: Agent failed to verify customer identity within the first 240 seconds, omitting requests for PIN, full billing address, or security question.

scorecard.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
scorecard.coaching: Agent failed to acknowledge customer's severe distress regarding being registered blind and threatened with debt collection due to unreadable 8-point print.

scorecard.name: Active listening
scorecard.coaching: Agent asked whether customer required Braille or Large Print at [10:15], ignoring customer's explicit statement in turn 1 that he needs Large Print.

scorecard.name: Took ownership of the problem
scorecard.coaching: Agent repeatedly disclaimed ownership, stating external print house contractors and commercial printing presses were not S-Net's responsibility.

scorecard.name: Probing
scorecard.coaching: Agent asked zero diagnostic questions regarding optical magnification point scales, high-contrast colours, or screen-reader formats.

grader.scenario: Visually impaired customer requesting Large Print bills; accessibility profile updated permanently; agent omits survey and closing branding, fails verification (never asks PIN/address/security question in 240s), ignores visual impairment distress, asks repeat question about Braille vs Large Print, disclaims billing print ownership, and asks zero probing questions
grader.notes: The agent enrolled a visually impaired customer onto the Priority Services Register and updated the billing delivery template to 24-point Large Print format. However, the agent failed Branding and Survey Check by omitting 'thank you for choosing s-net' and the survey, failed Verified Customer by never requesting PIN, address, or security question in the first 240 seconds, failed Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement by disregarding Patrick's acute distress over being registered blind and unable to read microscopic 8-point billing print, failed Active Listening at minute 11 by asking whether he required Braille or Large Print after Patrick explicitly stated in turn 1 that he needs Large Print, failed Took Ownership of the Problem by repeatedly disclaiming responsibility ('Third-party commercial printing contractors handle mailing; S-Net does not print bills in-house'), and failed Probing by asking zero diagnostic questions regarding font sizing, high-contrast layouts, or screen-reader formats.

items.name: Branding and Survey Check
items.evidence: [18:40] Agent: 'All accessibility preferences updated. Good afternoon and take care. Goodbye.' - Closing lacks mandatory S-Net branding and survey mention.

items.name: Verified customer
items.evidence: Agent requested only account reference and router model in the first 240 seconds, omitting required whole-word 'pin', 'address', or 'security question' verification.

items.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
items.evidence: [01:30] Customer: 'Rachel, last month I accidentally missed a payment deadline because I could not read the tiny payment due date... and S-Net slapped me with a late payment charge and threatened debt collection! I live alone with my guide dog and I have zero family nearby to read mail for me! Being treated like a delinquent debtor... is humiliating, terrifying, and deeply discriminatory!' Agent: 'Automated billing print runs default to standard twelve-pitch typeface...' - Total disregard of severe disability distress.

items.name: Paraphrasing
items.evidence: [01:45] Agent: 'So if I have understood correctly, your visual impairment makes standard paper billing print unreadable...' - Complete and accurate restatement.

items.name: Active listening
items.evidence: [10:15] Agent: 'Do you require your monthly bills in Grade 2 Braille or in Large Print format?' Customer: 'Rachel, as I explained at the very start of this call, I need Large Print twenty-four-point! I cannot read Braille...' - Agent asked for information already given.

items.name: Took ownership of the problem
items.evidence: [02:20] Agent: 'Third-party commercial printing contractors handle paper mailing; S-Net does not print billing statements in-house and holds zero liability...' and [17:40] Agent: 'If commercial contractors print small font again in future, do not blame S-Net customer service...' - Direct disclaimers of ownership.

items.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
items.evidence: [12:10] Agent: 'Obviously that confirms your visual accessibility accommodation is fully established under statutory disability standards, Patrick.' - Clear technical reassurance.

items.name: Probing
items.evidence: Agent asked zero probing questions regarding font size (such as 18pt vs 24pt), paper background contrast, or electronic screen-reader accessibility.
